title: How to Interview Architects in Westchester NY: What to Ask and What to Look For
excerpt: Choosing the right architect for your Westchester home project matters more than you think. Here's how to ask the right questions and spot what actually matters.
content:
You're planning a kitchen remodel in Scarsdale, or maybe a second-story addition in Mamaroneck. Either way, you know you need an architect. But how do you pick one from the dozens working across Westchester County? The truth is, most homeowners don't know what to look for when they sit down with an architect. They end up making decisions based on gut feeling or a pretty website. That's a mistake.

A good interview with an architect will tell you almost everything you need to know. It's not about pressure or salesmanship. It's about figuring out if this person understands your home, your vision, and the local building department process in your town.

Ask About Their Actual Credentials and Experience

Start simple. Ask if they're a licensed architect in New York State. Don't assume. A designer is not an architect. An architect has gone through years of training, exams, and continuing education. It matters.

Then ask what they've actually built in your area. Have they done work in Harrison, Rye, or Pelham Manor? Do they understand the permit process in White Plains versus Eastchester? Every Westchester municipality has its own building department and specific code requirements. An architect who's worked locally knows what questions to ask upfront and which inspectors care about which details.

Pay attention to how they describe past projects. If they can walk you through a home renovation in Westchester step by step and explain what went well and what they'd do differently, that's a sign they're thinking about real outcomes, not just the design phase.

Find Out if They're Actually Running Your Project

Here's a question most homeowners never ask: will you be the one on my job? Or will you hand it off to someone else?

The difference matters enormously. When a licensed architect in Westchester NY personally oversees your project from start to finish, you get consistent decision-making and accountability. You're not playing telephone between the design team, the construction team, and whoever is checking in on your addition in Dobbs Ferry or your historic restoration in Tarrytown.

Some firms work differently. That's fine. But you should know exactly how they operate before you hire them.

Ask How They Handle Permits and Building Departments

This is where a lot of homeowners get lost. The permit process can feel mysterious and scary. A good architect will treat it like a routine part of the job.

Ask how they work with your local building department. Ask if they pull the permits or if you do. Ask if they've dealt with issues during inspections before and how they solved them. An architect who's done a custom home in Westchester County or a home addition in Westchester knows that permits aren't obstacles. They're part of building something that's safe, legal, and will last.

Also ask if they handle revisions if the inspector flags something. Again, it happens. The question is whether your architect treats it as part of the service or as an extra charge.

Listen to How They Talk About Your Home

Pay attention to whether they ask questions or just talk. A residential architect in Scarsdale or anywhere else in the county should be curious about how you live in your house. Do you cook a lot? Do you work from home? Do you entertain? Do you want to open up walls or keep the spaces defined?

If they're already showing you their favorite design trends or pushing you toward their style, that's a red flag. Your home should reflect your needs and taste, not their portfolio.

Good architects listen more than they talk in the first meeting. They take notes. They ask for clarification. They seem genuinely interested in understanding your house and your life.
